notes: Correct and conservative (unknown names count as response conditions) with an updated doc comment and very thorough end-to-end tests for both retry and no-retry cases; somewhat more verbose than needed, with extra req-ident and member-call filtering.

Correct AST-based detection with an explicit all-names-known flag that treats unknown names conservatively, plus a doc update and strong table-driven retry tests including a body-replay regression; somewhat more verbose than needed.

The core fix is identical to the reference, but the patch also includes unrelated changes: a new production DetachAfterHijack method on IdleTimeoutWriter, network_proxy edits in the proxyprotocol integration tests, and a matching responsewriter test, which is a serious scope violation.

The core fix matches the reference exactly and the task tests are thorough, but the patch also ships an unrelated production change (IdleTimeoutWriter.DetachAfterHijack), an unrelated test for it, and unrelated proxyprotocol integration-test edits.

Source change matches the reference exactly, and the tests are thorough: a ph() variant of the status-code retry, the request-only cases (upstream.host, escaped literal, status_codes), and dynamic-name extraction.

Implementation is identical to the reference, and the focused tests cover shorthand vs ph() calls, escaped literals, look-alike names, upstream.host and dynamic names, both at the AST level and through end-to-end retries.

Correct AST-based extraction of placeholder names with a separate dynamic flag and the full response-placeholder set; minor nit that Placeholders() returns its internal slice uncloned, with solid unit and regression tests.
Correct and concise, using MatchDescendants with a dynamic flag, with good unit and runtime tests; it also leaves the LoadBalancing doc comment stale and returns the internal slice uncloned.

Clean ReferencesPlaceholder(predicate) API that treats dynamic names conservatively and covers the exact response placeholders, with a good classification table (macros, escaped literals, near-miss names) and a POST passthrough regression test.

Clean predicate-based API that tracks dynamic names, and the unit table covers macros, is_transport_error and look-alike names; however, the LoadBalancing doc comment was left stating that all expression sets are evaluated against responses.

Functionally correct but convoluted: squashfs New/NewObject retry with remote comparisons, a special-cased EOF hack in zip Open, and squashfs tests that depend on an external mksquashfs binary and may be skipped.

Functional, but the squashfs root detection (`expectedRemote`) and NewObject retry logic are convoluted, the zip seek-past-end special case applies only to symlinks, there is no shadow handling, and the squashfs test is skipped without the mksquashfs binary.

Works and is well tested, but adds extras the task did not ask for (root accepted without the suffix, a stat-based ErrorDirNotFound change in List), and squashfs root lookup can resolve 'x.rclonelink' to a regular file 'x'.

Works and shares a link reader helper, but adds an unrelated ErrorDirNotFound change and accepts roots without the suffix; its suffix-fallback lookup lets New() treat a root of `X.rclonelink` as the regular file `X`, and it does not handle shadowing.

Clean implementation close to the reference with shared archiver helpers (bounded target read, skip notice, range/seek-aware OpenLink) and correct NewObject/root fallback to the suffixed name, but a symlink clashing with a regular x.rclonelink member is not handled.

Close to the reference, with sensible shared helpers (bounded target read, unified skip notice, ranged reader), correct root-at-link handling and docs; it does not handle the symlink-vs-`.rclonelink` shadow case, but neither does the reference.

Clean approach that adds symlinks after regular entries so they cannot take a name already in use, handles singleObject roots correctly, and has thorough backend-level and archive-level tests including the skip notice and hostile copy.

Clean implementation that adds symlinks after regular entries so a real `.rclonelink` member keeps its name in both backends, with consistent NewObject lookup, a correct root-at-link path, and good tests including log-notice and hostile-copy checks.

Focused fix for both backends that keeps regular .rclonelink members from being shadowed by symlinks, keeps listing and NewObject consistent, handles a root pointing at a link, and adds a sensible docs section.

Correct fix for both backends that matches the reference, adds docs, and goes further by stopping a symlink from shadowing a real `.rclonelink` member so List and NewObject agree; tests are thorough, though the zip `remote`→`name` rename adds some churn.

Over-engineered case-insensitive LinkFilter that drops symlinks with members inside them (one hidden test fails) and can also drop regular .rclonelink members, while squashfs NewObject now builds the whole directory listing on every lookup.

The new case-insensitive LinkFilter abstraction drops links that contain members (failing a hidden test) and even hides regular `.rclonelink` files on clash, contrary to the spec; squashfs NewObject now reads every entry and link target in the directory.

Zip and squashfs symlinks are exposed as .rclonelink objects, but the zip side drops any symlink that has members 'inside' it or clashes with another name, which loses the hostile-archive symlink the expected behaviour keeps (one hidden test fails), and the addLinks clash pass adds complexity.

Drops any symlink that has a member inside it instead of exposing it faithfully, which fails a hidden test; it also eagerly decompresses every zip symlink at listing time and edits the dirtree map directly with nil placeholders in `addLinks`.

Refcounted master-fd redesign that only unlinks its own map entry and cleans up the pool on error; it seems sound, but it is an over-broad refactor (including a redundant atomic under the mutex) that breaks all hidden tests.
A sound ref-counted master-fd design that also handles NUL-prefixed names and cleans up the pool on File() errors, but it fails all hidden tests and its abstract-socket tests check the wrong path.

Essentially matches the reference: it closes the leaked intermediate dup fd, drops the File() call in Close, holds unixSocketsMu across decrement/close/unlink, adds a CAS closed flag returning net.ErrClosed, and skips abstract names; the only minor deviation is that the '@' check lacks a GOOS guard.

Closely matches the reference: it closes the leaked dup, stops the File() leak in Close, unlinks the stored address under the lock, and adds a closed guard returning ErrClosed; the only gaps are the abstract check ignoring GOOS and a weak abstract test.

Plausibly correct, with the lock held across close and release, but it heavily rewrites listenReusable with unconditional type assertions, changes deleteListener semantics, and edits listeners.go; hidden tests all fail.

The redesign fixes the leak, but its added close-on-chmod-failure in listeners.go calls a Close that locks unixSocketsMu while Listen already holds it, which self-deadlocks; it also fails all hidden tests.

The master-fd plus refcounted unixSocket redesign looks behaviorally sound (it even fixes reuse after closing the newest holder), but it rewrites the map type, listenReusable flow and deleteListener receivers, breaking every hidden test.

A similar ref-counted redesign that looks functionally correct, but it fails all hidden tests, the abstract check ignores GOOS, and its abstract-socket test uses a decoy file without the '@' so it proves nothing.

A separate state mutex and master-fd refcount look race-safe, but it also changes listenerPool counting for reused sockets (affecting shutdown-delay logic), wraps reuse returns differently, and edits listeners.go; all hidden tests fail.

The logic works, but it adds a second mutex, changes listenerPool counting for reused sockets (which affects shutdown-delay behavior) and edits listeners.go, all well beyond the issue, and it fails all hidden tests.

A clean master-fd refcount design with a GOOS-aware abstract check that appears correct, but the large internal restructuring (map type, pointer deleteListener) is incompatible with the expected code, so hidden tests fail entirely.

A shared 'master fd' redesign fixes the leak, the unlink and double-close, and correctly guards abstract sockets by GOOS; the logic looks sound, but rewriting the internal structs broke all hidden tests and makes the patch far larger than needed.
